To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the calix[arene] platform is a valuable building block for the design of luminescent probes, and that the aggregation state of the molecule in solution has a strong impact on the luminescent properties.

(i) TbIII-DOTA-functionalized calix[4]-arenes are efficient lanthanide luminescent materials; (ii) the presence of a phthalimido group in the lower rim of the calixarene enhances luminescence quantum yields; and (iii) luminescence properties are highly dependent on the aggregation behavior of the calix-arenes in solution.

the calix[arene core is an efficient sensitizer of TbIII-centered luminescence, the luminescence of TbIII-DOTAs in solution is concentration dependent, and the critical micelle concentrations of the compounds are variable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of new luminescent lanthanide complexes with potential applications as MRI probes.
the design, synthesis and characterization of luminescent lanthanide complexes with calix[4]-based ligands.
the synthesis of new luminescent calyx[4]arenetetraamide complexes and with the study of their photophysical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calix[arene] platform is an efficient sensitizer for lanthanide luminescence in both solid state and solution.
the luminescence efficiency of TbIII-DTPA-calix[4]-arene-3-OPr-OPht is higher in solid state, while the efficiency of TbIII-DO3A-calix[3]arene-1,3-OPr is higher in solution.
the calix[3]arenes with a phthalimidyl group in the upper rim and with a propyl group in the lower one, are the most promising candidates for the design of luminescent probes for optical imaging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the luminescent properties of the TbIII-DOTA-functionalized calix[4](3,5-diamino)arenes are determined by the aggregation behavior of the compounds in solution, and the aggregation behavior in turn is determined by the substituent on the lower rim of the calixarene.

the calix[5]arene scaffold can be considered a versatile platform for the design of multimodal contrast agents, with the possibility to combine the high relaxivity of GdIII- with the high luminescence efficiency of TbIII.

calix[4]-arenes can act as a versatile scaffold to combine the properties of lanthanide complexes with the properties of chromophores, and to tune the luminescent properties of the resulting complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calix[4]-based platforms can be used to modulate the luminescence quantum yields of TbIII-DOTAs.
the presence of a chromophore on the lower rim of the calixarene is not sufficient to sensitize TbIII-luminescence in solution.
the presence of an aromatic group in the lower rim of a TbIII-calix[4]-arene complex does not necessarily lead to a higher Tb-centered quantum yield.
